name: determinizing-guest-yardstick
question: Can a guest with an invariant true BY CONSTRUCTION hold that invariant natively, including under ~20x parallel stress, well enough to serve as a golden yardstick for later backend parity comparison?
answer: Yes for guest_k_syscalls (exactly 10000 getpid, 20/20 under stress). The validation gate is proven to discriminate: a load-dependent guest passed the single-run check and was rejected only by the stress check.
counted_by: strace -c (ptrace-based; corroboration only, NOT the golden reference)
golden_signal: guest self-check exit code, which needs no external observer

artifacts.guest_k_syscalls.c: ACCEPTED guest #1: freestanding, static, nostdlib; exactly K=10000 getpid then exit_group
artifacts.guest_rejected_nondet.c: REJECTED: time-bounded loop; sched_yield count is load-dependent
artifacts.guest_rejected.c: REJECTED: libc/stdio; count is a function of buffering and environment
artifacts.validate_guest.sh: the gate: G1 exit code, G2 count, G3 environment invariance, G4 20x parallel

backends_compared: NONE - deliberately out of scope; this task validates the instrument only
